Description: Discovered a potential basic authorization token provided in a curl command, which could compromise the curl accessed resource.
Author: Drew (DevOps Automation)
Message:
feat(observability): alerting, log data governance, and Grafana access control

Alerting: Alertmanager plus four version-controlled rules, replacing "a
human looks at a dashboard" with a reproducible verdict. Two rules encode
non-obvious correctness. Blue/green makes a naive `up == 0` wrong -- the
parked colour is *supposed* to be down, so the rule aggregates with
`sum(up{...}) == 0`; the first version was observed entering `pending` on
the idle colour within minutes. And an unguarded error ratio yields NaN at
zero traffic, so the alert looks armed while being incapable of firing in
exactly the low-traffic conditions where a bad deploy hides.

check_health.sh gives a scheduled agent a graded exit code (0/1/2/3). Exit 3
is the reason it exists: a dead Prometheus reports zero active alerts and so
does a healthy one, so the checker refuses to read an empty alert list as
good news until it has proven something was watching.

Also fixed a real hole: production-like was not scraped at all. The
environment carrying traffic had zero monitoring while develop had full
coverage.

Log data governance, in order: classify (services declare
platform.data_class via a Docker label -- declarative, not a hardcoded list
that goes stale), redact (at WRITE time; a query-time filter is a promise
that everyone will remember it, and once an unmasked identifier is stored
the only remedy is rebuilding the store), separate (different Loki TENANTS,
not labels -- a label can be filtered out by a query someone chooses not to
write, a tenant is enforced on every request). Restricted data is retained
for LESS time, not more: how long sensitive material exists is itself a
control. Redaction is v1: three high-confidence patterns, and it will not
catch free-text names or unexpected formats.

Disk pressure is guarded in two places because they fail differently: Loki
limits protect Loki, Docker json-file rotation protects the host disk.

Grafana anonymous access is off. The trap this closes:
GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD is only honoured on FIRST database init, so on an
existing volume it is silently ignored. Setting it and stopping there is
worse than doing nothing -- it converts "everyone is a viewer" into "anyone
who tries admin/admin is an admin" while the config reads as locked down.
Observed exactly that. The script now resets the live password and asserts
both that the Vault credential works and that admin/admin no longer does.

Verified by generating real PII: the stored line is fully masked,
cross-tenant queries return zero rows, and a query with no X-Scope-OrgID is
rejected 401. Alerting verified by stopping containers, not by reading
config.
